\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ساک} (sâk)}{ساک (sâk)}]{\fa{ساک} (sâk) — a holdall, a travel bag}

\label{lesson:FA-C433-sak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to search, then the Persian for a flight attendant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ساک}}
\textbf{\fa{ساک}} (\emph{sâk}) — \textquotedblleft{}a holdall, a travel bag\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{یک} \fa{ساک} \fa{کوچک} \fa{برای} \fa{سفر} \fa{کافی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Yek sâk-e kuchek barâ-ye safar kâfi ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A small bag is enough for the trip.
\end{quote}

\emph{Sâk-e varzeshi} — a sports bag.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sâk} was borrowed from French and is usually traced to French \emph{sac} 'bag'. EtymDB does not list the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sâk}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sâk}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sâk}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to search, then the Persian for a flight attendant, then say \emph{sâk} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بار} \fa{بستن} (bâr bastan)}{بار بستن (bâr bastan)}]{\fa{بار} \fa{بستن} (bâr bastan) — to pack (for a journey)}

\label{lesson:FA-C433-bar-bastan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a flight attendant, then the Persian for a holdall.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بار} \fa{بستن}}
\textbf{\fa{بار} \fa{بستن}} (\emph{bâr bastan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to pack (for a journey)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شب} \fa{قبل} \fa{از} \fa{سفر} \fa{بار} \fa{بستیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Shab-e qabl az safar bâr bastim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We packed the night before the trip.
\end{quote}

\emph{bâr} 'load' + \emph{bastan} 'to tie'. Present stem \emph{band-}: \emph{bâr mibandim}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâr bastan} is built from native \emph{bâr} 'load', which EtymDB lists, and \emph{bastan} 'to tie, to bind', which EtymDB traces to the PIE root \emph{b\textsuperscript{h}end\textsuperscript{h}-} 'to bind'. Loads were once tied onto pack animals.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâr bastan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâr bastan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâr bastan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a flight attendant, then the Persian for a holdall, then say \emph{bâr bastan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{بار} \fa{بستن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pack (for a journey)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بدرقه} \fa{کردن} (badraqe kardan)}{بدرقه کردن (badraqe kardan)}]{\fa{بدرقه} \fa{کردن} (badraqe kardan) — to see off (someone leaving)}

\label{lesson:FA-C433-badraqe-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a holdall, then the Persian for to pack.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بدرقه} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{بدرقه} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{badraqe kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to see off (someone leaving)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{ما} \fa{را} \fa{تا} \fa{ایستگاه} \fa{بدرقه} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâdaram mâ râ tâ istgâh badraqe kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother saw us off at the station.
\end{quote}

\emph{badraqe} 'a send-off' + \emph{kardan}. Iranian families often see travellers off with water poured behind them.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{badraqe kardan} is built from \emph{badraqe} 'a send-off, an escort', whose origin is not settled, and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badraqe kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badraqe kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{badraqe kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a holdall, then the Persian for to pack, then say \emph{badraqe kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{بدرقه} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To see off (someone leaving)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{استقبال} \fa{کردن} (esteqbâl kardan)}{استقبال کردن (esteqbâl kardan)}]{\fa{استقبال} \fa{کردن} (esteqbâl kardan) — to meet (someone arriving), to welcome}

\label{lesson:FA-C433-esteqbal-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to pack, then the Persian for to see off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{استقبال} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{استقبال} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{esteqbâl kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to meet (someone arriving), to welcome\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دوستانم} \fa{در} \fa{فرودگاه} \fa{از} \fa{من} \fa{استقبال} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dustânam dar forudgâh az man esteqbâl kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My friends met me at the airport.
\end{quote}

The person met takes \emph{az}: \emph{az u esteqbâl kardim}. Also to welcome an idea.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{esteqbâl kardan} is built from \emph{esteqbâl} 'a welcome', borrowed from Arabic \emph{istiqbāl}, which EtymDB derives from \emph{istaqbala} 'to receive, to meet, to face', and \emph{kardan} 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esteqbâl kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esteqbâl kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{esteqbâl kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to pack, then the Persian for to see off, then say \emph{esteqbâl kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عجله} \fa{کردن} ('ajale kardan)}{عجله کردن ('ajale kardan)}]{\fa{عجله} \fa{کردن} ('ajale kardan) — to hurry, to be in a hurry}

\label{lesson:FA-C433-ajale-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to see off, then the Persian for to meet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عجله} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{عجله} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{'ajale kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to hurry, to be in a hurry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{عجله} \fa{کردیم} \fa{ولی} \fa{قطار} \fa{رفته} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{'Ajale kardim vali qatâr rafte bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We hurried, but the train had gone.
\end{quote}

\emph{'ajale} 'haste' + \emph{kardan}. \emph{'Ajale dâshtan} — to be in a hurry.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'ajale kardan} is built from \emph{'ajale} 'haste', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{ʿajala} 'haste', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
